question: Why do we make sure hospital beds are free of wrinkles and crumbs?

options.A: To reduce the physical weight of the mattress during turns
options.B: To prevent skin irritation and pressure sores
options.C: To make it easier to transfer patients to a wheelchair
options.D: To comply with dietary and housekeeping rules

explanation: Great job! Tiny crumbs and creases put constant pressure on fragile patient skin, which quickly turns into painful bedsores. Keeping the bed smooth is a vital part of nursing care! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why is simple bed making considered an essential clinical nursing skill rather than just housekeeping?

options.A: It is the only duty a nursing student can do alone
options.B: It replaces the need for daily patient bathing
options.C: It directly promotes patient comfort, safety, and skin integrity
options.D: It lowers the overall room temperature for fever management

explanation: Spot on! A clean, well-made bed is the foundation of a safe healing environment. It protects vulnerable skin and keeps your patients comfortable. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why must a nurse avoid shaking clean or dirty bed sheets in a hospital ward?

options.A: It causes the cotton fibers to tear and stretch
options.B: It creates static electricity that damages monitors
options.C: It violates facility laundry sorting protocols
options.D: It spreads dust and germs into the surrounding air

explanation: You got it! Shaking sheets sends dust, skin flakes, and bacteria flying into the air, where they can settle on other patients or clean surfaces. Always fold or roll them gently instead! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h2)

question: Where should you put a heavily soiled bed sheet immediately after removing it from the mattress?

options.A: On the clean bedside chair until you finish the bed
options.B: On the clean floor near the foot of the bed temporarily
options.C: Folded neatly on the overbed table for later sorting
options.D: Directly into a designated laundry hamper or bag

explanation: That's right! Putting dirty linen straight into a hamper stops germs from spreading to the floor, furniture, or your uniform. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a draw sheet placed across the middle of a hospital bed?

options.A: To replace the need for a standard bottom sheet
options.B: To help lift, turn, and reposition the patient easily
options.C: To serve as an extra blanket during cold night shifts
options.D: To catch food crumbs during meal delivery times

explanation: Correct! A draw sheet acts like a handy helper, letting you slide or turn a patient smoothly without causing friction burns or shear injuries. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h3)

question: When gathering supplies to make an empty bed, where is the safest place to put your clean linen stack?

options.A: On a clean bedside chair, never on another patient's bed
options.B: Directly on the clean floor to keep your hands free
options.C: Held tightly against your uniform while walking
options.D: Stacked on top of the patient's meal tray for easy reach

explanation: Spot on! Keeping clean linen on a chair or clean table stops it from picking up germs from the floor or other units. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h3)

question: When stripping a dirty bed, what is the correct way to handle the used linen?

options.A: Roll it inward toward the center to trap dirt and microbes
options.B: Shake each sheet vigorously to remove loose hair
options.C: Toss the bundle across the room into the laundry chute
options.D: Fold each sheet into a square and place on the floor

explanation: You nailed it! Rolling the dirty linen inward traps skin flakes, dust, and germs so they don't fly into the air or onto your clothes. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why do nurses make mitered corners when tucking in hospital bed sheets?

options.A: To create a neat, secure fit that prevents sheets from pulling loose
options.B: To allow air to circulate freely around the patient's feet
options.C: To make it easier to fold the mattress in half for storage
options.D: To comply with international hotel standards for hospital rooms

explanation: Correct! Mitered corners lock the bedding tightly in place, meaning restless patient movement won't easily pull the sheets untucked. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the most important safety action before turning a patient to one side during an occupied bed change?

options.A: Lock the bed wheels and lower the mattress to the floor
options.B: Ask a family member to hold the patient's legs steady
options.C: Raise the side rail on the opposite side of the bed
options.D: Administer a mild sedative to keep the patient calm

explanation: Well done! Raising the opposite side rail creates a physical barrier so the patient won't accidentally roll right out of bed while you work. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h5)

question: When changing sheets for a bedridden patient who cannot get up, how should you handle the top covers?

options.A: Place the clean top sheet over the old one, then pull the old sheet out from underneath
options.B: Ask the patient to hold the dirty blanket up with both hands
options.C: Remove all covers completely, leaving the patient uncovered until the end
options.D: Strip the top of the bed first and replace sheets while the patient sits up

explanation: Spot on! Layering the clean cover over the old one before sliding the old one out keeps your patient warm and protects their privacy the whole time. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why must you always lower a hospital bed to its lowest position after finishing a bed change?

options.A: To comply with fire safety codes for emergency exits
options.B: To reduce the risk of injury if the patient tries to get out of bed
options.C: To allow the mechanical bed motor to cool down
options.D: To make it easier for the cleaning crew to mop underneath

explanation: You got it! A low bed minimizes the fall distance if an unassisted patient tries to climb out, protecting them from serious head injuries or broken bones. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which item must always be placed within a patient's easy reach before you leave the room after making their bed?

options.A: The room key and visitor pass
options.D: The clinical chart and nursing clipboard

explanation: Correct! The call light is your patient's lifeline to ask for help. Keeping it close by prevents dangerous attempts to climb out of bed unassisted. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h6)
